newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil alcohol fuel car output hits record low.
newsitem.headline: Brazil alcohol fuel car output hits record low.

text.p: Brazil produced 8,737 alcohol fuel vehicles between January and November 1996, or 0.6 percent of total output in the period, Brazil's Motor Manufacturers Association Anfavea said.
Alcohol fuel car output in 1996 is likely to drop to its lowest level since production of the cars began in 1979, an Anfavea spokesman said.

In 1985, production of alcohol fuel cars reached a record high of 647,445 vehicles, accounting for 84.8 percent of total vehicle output in Brazil that year. Production of alcohol fuel cars began falling in the late eighties as government enthusiasm for the pro-alcohol campaign began to wane, resulting in fuel supply problems.
Anfavea will hold a news conference on Jan 9 to release car production figures for gasoline and alcohol fuel cars in 1996 and production estimates for 1997.
